item.title: NDC and the battle within
item.description: By Hussein Yahaya, Abuja; Sani Ibrahim Paki & Salim Umar Ibrahim, Kano With 81 days to the January 16, 2027 presidential elections, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is enmeshed in a fresh crisis over the composition of its presidential campaign council. The NDC on Sunday unveiled its national campaign council, appointing Ibrahim Abdulkarim as its Director-General and the NDC National Secretary, Ikenna Enekweizu, as the council’s secretary. Under the structure, the NDC National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, will serve as the chairman of the council; the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will serve as co-chairman; Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe (NDC National Chairman) is the vice-chairman, while Rabiu Kwankwaso, the party’s vice-presidential candidate, is the co-vice chairman. The council also features prominent figures including former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, heading the National Advisory Council, former Deputy Senate President Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Pat Utomi, and Buba Galadima. Daily Trust reports that no sooner had the NDC unveiled its council than the OK (Obi-Kwankwaso) Movement launched an attack on the party, saying the list casts serious doubt on the party’s readiness for the upcoming general elections. Analyst say for the NDC to get its acts right ahead of the elections, it must clearly define the extent of how the diehard supporters of their presidential and vice presidential candidates could influence decisions. In a statement issued in Abuja, Director-General of the OK Movement, John Ughulu, criticised the NDC leadership for dragging its feet in mobilising its electoral machinery, warning that political ambition without ground-level coordination portends defeat. “With less than three months until the general elections, they are only just announcing their Presidential Campaign Council,” Ughulu said. “What exactly have they been doing all this time? Where is the structure? Where is the strategy? Where is the machinery required to prosecute a serious national election?” Taking a jab at the composition of the campaign list, Ughulu boasted that the OK Movement had already completed the heavy lifting required for victory, predicting that the party elite would soon seek assistance. The fresh wave of criticism underlines a widening rift between the NDC leadership and the OK Movement over control and campaign strategy for Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso. The OK Movement had, in September, unveiled a 59-member Presidential Campaign Council comprising zonal and state coordinators, as well as directors overseeing various aspects of the campaign, but the party dissociated itself from the list, saying a support group did not have the right to constitute a campaign council for the party. The resultant friction in the internal workings of the party is yet to abate, with the movement objecting to the naming of a national campaign council by the party on Monday. item.title: [UPDATED] Kane Edges Yamal, Mbappe To Taste Ballon d’Or Glory
item.description: Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native London on Monday, beating stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time, extending Spain’s dominance of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first-ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date. England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane smiles after receiving the Ballon d’Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. “Without you guys (his Bayern Munich teammates) and the rest of the team it wouldn’t be possible; the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much,” he said after collecting the award. Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas (centre) and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane (right) pose after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football. “Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier. “Some people saw it as a risk, but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the teammates, the team, the club, and it has pushed me onto another level. “Being a number nine for Bayern and England, you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added. The Bayern Munich striker emerged as the standout player at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, held on Monday, October 26, after an outstanding year for club and country. item.title: [UPDATED] Alexia Putellas Wins 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or
item.description: Alexia Putellas picked up her third Ballon d’Or in her new home city of London on Monday, crowning a spectacular return to the top of women’s football after injury cut her down in her prime. Putellas previously picked up the prize for the best player in the world in 2021 and 2022 as the creative heartbeat of an all-conquering Barcelona side. But an anterior cruciate ligament tear just as she was preparing for Spain’s bid to win Euro 2022 derailed her rise to global stardom. Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane pose with their trophies on stage after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) Putellas recovered to play a bit part role in Spain’s World Cup triumph a year later, but was overshadowed by teammate Aitana Bonmatí for both club and country as it took nearly two years to rediscover her best form. “Ever since I suffered the injury, I’ve been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it’ll happen again,” Putellas told AFP in an interview last month. Bonmati took on the mantle of the world’s best player, becoming a three-time Ballon d’Or winner between 2023 and 2025 until she was also sidelined by a leg break. With the emphasis back on Putellas, she rose to the challenge, helping Barcelona regain the Champions League last season in dominant fashion. “I never felt that the (Ballon d’Or) trophy was ‘mine’… Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now,” she added. Having achieved all that she could in Catalonia, Putellas embarked on a new adventure, joining London City Lionesses. Owned by American businesswoman Michele Kang, the Lionesses are aiming to break the mould as the only fully independent team in England’s top division. “It’s a complete change in my life. It’s a constant, daily learning process: the culture, the language, moving to a new country, a new city,” said the 32-year-old. “I knew that if I ever had to end my time at Barca, it wouldn’t make much sense to repeat what I’d already experienced in the next chapter, mainly because it’s impossible. “It had to be something completely different. It’s practically a brand-new club, with everything yet to be written, so I’m trying to bring that winning culture and mentality with me.” The Putellas effect is already being felt in the English Women’s Super League with the Lionesses sat just behind Chelsea and Manchester City at the top of the table and ahead of traditional giants Arsenal. The move could also benefit Spain’s chances of retaining the World Cup next year with their star player facing a lesser workload without European football this season. “It was one of the things I took into account. item.title: Trump hits back at Obama over Saddam ‘Cheesecake Factory’ jab
item.description: US President Donald Trump hit back at Barack Obama on Monday after the former president jokingly said his successor’s White House looked as if it were a cheesecake restaurant run by Saddam Hussein. “For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president,” Trump said in a three-minute diatribe when asked about Obama’s comments over the weekend. “Guys like Obama, they would pass the front door, they would see the broken masonry… He doesn’t notice dirt and filth where the walls haven’t been cleaned for years,” Trump told reporters as he headed for his latest midterm election rally. Cheesecake Factory is a popular restaurant chain known for its lengthy list of indulgent dishes and an eclectic interior design. Obama made a series of scathing criticisms of Republican Trump’s “chaos and cruelty” as he hit the stump for Democrats in Ohio and Michigan ahead of next week’s midterm elections. But it was Obama’s jabs at billionaire Trump’s prized renovations at the White House — including building a massive ballroom and adding gold-leafed ornamentation throughout the Oval Office — that really appeared to sting. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said on Saturday, referring to the Iraqi dictator who was executed in 2006 following the US invasion of Iraq. Trump has long had a bitter rivalry with Obama. He launched his own political career by pushing the racist and false “birther” conspiracy theory that the Democrat was lying about being born in the United States. But Trump’s rant over the cheesecake comments was also a sign of the 80-year-old’s increasingly short temper as the midterms loom. On Sunday night, Trump sent his longest ever post on his Truth Social network — a 1,300-word screed in which he railed not about Iran or the economy but about US comedian Bill Maher. Last week Trump also lashed out at a series of reporters as he faced questions about the midterms, in which Republicans face losing control of Congress, and his dealings with Russia. item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Spain’s Luis de la Fuente wins men’s Coach of the Year award
item.description: Spain national team manager Luis de la Fuente has won the Men’s Coach of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony after leading Spain to victory at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. De la Fuente emerged victorious ahead of fellow nominees Mikel Arteta of Arsenal, Luis Enrique of Paris Saint-Germain, Vincent Kompany of Bayern Munich and Unai Emery of Aston Villa. Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez presented the award, although the announcement was briefly interrupted by an unexpected mix-up involving the winner’s name on the card. Benitez eventually announced De la Fuente as the winner, prompting the Spanish coach to shake hands with Emery and Spain international Lamine Yamal before making his way to the stage. The award adds to De la Fuente’s achievements with the Spanish national team, following Spain’s triumph at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. item.title: [UPDATED] Ebola: Nigeria Has 54 Primary Contacts Now, Many Are In Quarantine, Says NCDC
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) on Monday said that it has identified another contact linked to the confirmed case of the recent Ebola outbreak in Nigeria, increasing the number of primary contacts to 54. The Director-General of the agency, Dr. Jide Idris, disclosed this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , identifying the new contact as an e-hailing driver who drove the index patient. “So as it is now, we’ve had — yesterday it was 54, right? One has left. The index case has left, so we had 53. “Today, we got one more suspected case contact, who actually was the Uber driver who actually drove her again before to the first hospital. That information we got later,” he said. ﻿ Idris explained that many of the contacts were in quarantine, including six who self-quarantined at home. “So we still have 54 contacts, primary contacts. What we do is that we follow up with these people because a lot of them are in quarantine right now somewhere in Abuja, here, about 40-something of them.” “We have six that are home, self-quarantined because the risks appear low. But they monitor them, call them, take their temperature, morning, evening, just to ensure that there are no changes in clinical situation. “And one or two cases like that we had. He changes. And we had to do, we had to test them again. And the three of them again today were tested, and all the three of them turned out negative,” he added. Not Out Of The Woods The NCDC chief also said efforts were ongoing to identify the secondary contacts. “So we are not out of the woods yet until we are sure that we have all the contacts, and they have been followed up. So we are still not out of the woods; because the index case is out doesn’t mean that we don’t have that,” added. The DG further said that though Nigeria does not have an active positive case, there are contacts that the agency needs to follow up. “Anyone who is symptomatic will test to be sure. You have to follow them for between two and 21 days. That’s the incubation period. And again, after 21 days, you follow up 21 days again. You take it to that before you say, OK, this is Ebola-free,” Idris said. “And after 21 days you test again, it’s negative, you can allow them to go. For secondary contacts, we don’t know how many until we start taking them.” Asked what anyone who experiences symptoms should do, the DG said, “Contact the nearest public health centre. There is an NCDC number: 6232. It is a hotline. item.title: NDC opens new Abuja base, targets 2027 electoral victory
item.description: …As Dickson hails new national secretariat as Noah’s Ark 2 By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has inaugurated its newly acquired national secretariat in Abuja as part of efforts to strengthen its operations ahead of the 2027 general election. The facility, located in the Jabi area of the Federal Capital Territory, was unveiled shortly after an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), as it marks a significant step in the party’s efforts to strengthen its organisational structure and establish a permanent administrative base as preparations for the forthcoming elections gather momentum. The new secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative centre and headquarters for its presidential campaign as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, just as the development marks a step in the NDC’s efforts to establish a permanent national base for coordinating its activities and managing its expanding political structure. It is a strategic centre for coordinating its activities, strengthening communication among state chapters and mobilising supporters across the country and is also expected to play a central role in organising the party’s presidential campaign and coordinating other electoral activities ahead of the 2027 general elections In his remarks, the National Leader of the party, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the facility as its new “Noah’s Ark” ahead of the 2027 general elections as he congratulated members and supporters on the acquisition, describing the new secretariat as a unifying centre that would provide a befitting home for the party’s growing membership. He referred to the facility as the NDC’s newly acquired “Noah’s Ark,” a description underscoring its importance as a rallying point for members and supporters as the party pursues its political ambitions. The inauguration attracted the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas; National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson; and Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly. Also present was the party’s Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, alongside other party leaders and members. With this, the NDC has positioned itself as an alternative political platform for Nigerians seeking a change from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). With the new facility, the party is expected to strengthen coordination between its national leadership, state chapters and other structures as election preparations continue. item.title: OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have neutralised 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters during coordinated air and artillery strikes on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad, following intelligence on the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters. According to the Joint Task Force, the operation followed sustained and relentless offensive against terrorist networks in the Lake Chad Basin. “The operation was conducted between 1 am and 2 am on 26 October 2026, using air and ground weapon systems to engage the identified locations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicates that 16 ISWAP fighters were neutralised across the targeted locations. “Among those reportedly killed were Abu Zubiru, an Arab national, and two associates, Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq, alongside other fighters. “Additionally, Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven others. “Operation Hadin Kai reaffirms that there is no hiding place for terrorists and remains committed to restoring peace and normalcy while conducting intelligence-led operations against terrorist elements in the North East. “Members of the public are encouraged to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations.” The post OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
item.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence. Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centers, sales and marketing, are excluded. “The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo. It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year. In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early. Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC. Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings. Around 27 percent of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer. The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week. item.title: Niger APC raises 525-member campaign council, targets 2m votes for Tinubu/Bago
item.description: By Clare Nnabuike Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago has declared that his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), is targeting 2 million votes to defeat the opposition parties in the 2027 presidential and governorship elections. The governor made this known on Monday at the inauguration of a 525-member State Presidential/Gubernatorial Campaign Council of the APC in Minna, where he revealed that the council is drawn from commissioners, special advisers, local government chairmen, councillors, state and national lawmakers, ministers, directors-general and coordinators. Bago described the structure as spanning party units to the state level and including political appointees, with total membership exceeding 100,000 over the years. “If everybody would bring its own votes, it would give us more than 1 million votes. But our target is beyond that. The ambition this time around is to bring out over 2 million votes, and by the grace of God we will do that,” he said. The governor urged the party to welcome returnees who had earlier defected to other parties, crediting the APC’s emergence as a coalition of parties that defeated the main opposition. He called for constructive media coverage and warned against overheating the polity or triggering insecurity, saying the campaign would highlight the federal government’s economic policies, improved revenue and job creation. Bago cited recent infrastructure and security gains, including better roads and freer movement of goods in parts of the state, as part of what the government has done and disclosed that the North Central Presidential Campaign office in Minna would be commissioned next week, with possible attendance of the President, Vice President, Senate President, Speaker or National Chairman. Minister of Information, Idris Malagi, in his remarks, praised the choice of leadership of the council and said the APC would campaign on the administration’s record of transforming the Nigerian economy over the past three and a half years. He urged the newly appointed members to prioritise the collective good of the state and party unity The chairman of the APC North Central, Hon. Mu’azu Rijau, while congratulating the council leadership, stressed that the 2027 campaign council should not underestimate opponents, saying the party aimed to re-elect Governor Bago alongside its senators, House of Representatives members and state assembly members. Director-General of the campaign council, Ahmed Ibeto, accepted the assignment on behalf of members, pledging hard work, strategic coordination, grassroots engagement, unity, discipline and compliance with electoral guidelines. He said the council would establish operational frameworks across directorates, local governments, wards and units, and would value experience while welcoming new ideas. item.title: Temwa Chawinga becomes first African woman to finish in Ballon d’Or top 10
item.description: Malawian forward Temwa Chawinga has made history by becoming the first African woman to finish in the top 10 of the women’s Ballon d’Or. Chawinga’s achievement marks a significant milestone for African women’s football, placing the Malawi international among the world’s leading female players. Born on September 20, 1998, in Rumphi District, Malawi, Chawinga plays as a forward for Kansas City Current and the Malawi national team. She has enjoyed considerable success at club level, winning four Chinese Women’s Super League titles with Wuhan Jianghan University in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023. She also won the NWSL x Liga MX Femenil Summer Cup in 2024 and the NWSL Shield in 2025 with Kansas City Current. Her individual honours include two consecutive NWSL Most Valuable Player awards in 2024 and 2025, as well as two NWSL Golden Boots in the same years. Chawinga also claimed the Chinese Women’s Super League Golden Boot in 2022 and 2023 before winning the International Federation of Football History and Statistics (IFFHS) World’s Best Top Goal Scorer award in 2023. She was joined in the Ballon d’Or top 10 by Haiti’s Melchie Dumornay, Norway’s Caroline Graham Hansen, Spain’s Patri Guijarro, Denmark’s Pernille Harder, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, Spain’s Clàudia Pina and Alexia Putellas, England’s Alessia Russo, and Jamaica’s Khadija Shaw. The list features players from Europe, Africa and the Caribbean, reflecting the growing global reach of women’s football. Chawinga’s historic finish represents a breakthrough for African representation in the prestigious individual award and further highlights her rise as one of the leading figures in the women’s game. item.title: Police confirm man, teenager swept away by flood in Aba
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Police Command has confirmed that a man who attempted to rescue a teenage girl from a water-filled ditch at Faulks Road, Aba, was swept away alongside the girl during Sunday’s downpour. The Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this while responding to Vanguard inquiries, confirming that the incident occurred around the popular Ukwu Mango area of the commercial city. Chinaka said the tragedy happened near an ongoing construction site where an uncovered ditch had filled with rainwater. According to her, the teenage girl was passing through the area when she reportedly hit a stone and fell into the ditch. An adult who witnessed the incident reportedly plunged into the water in an attempt to rescue her, but both were swept away. “Unfortunately, we have not been able to see them. The police are aware, and the matter has been reported. Efforts are in place to see how they can be rescued,” Chinaka said. She confirmed that the two victims had yet to be found as search efforts continued. Asked whether the construction company responsible for the site would face possible charges over negligence, the police spokesperson said investigations were ongoing. The tragedy has raised concerns about the safety of construction sites during heavy rainfall, particularly where excavations and drainage channels are left uncovered and become submerged in floodwater. Aba’s flat terrain makes parts of the commercial city vulnerable to flooding during heavy downpours, increasing the risks posed by waterlogged roads, open drains and excavations. item.title: Impunity, justice system failure fuelling violence in North Central — Osinbajo
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Former Vice President of Nigeria, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, has attributed the widespread insecurity in North Central Nigeria and other parts of the country to failures in the justice system and inadequate punitive measures for crimes committed. Osinbajo stated this on Monday in Plateau State at a forum titled, “Countering Polarisation and Rebuilding Civic Cohesion in North Central Nigeria Beyond Tribe and Faith, Reclaiming Our Shared Stories,” organised by Justice Research Institute, JRI, in partnership with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, NIPSS. The former Vice President said, “Impunity destroys the fabric of society. There must be clear and enforceable consequences for wrongdoing and offences committed against the state or individuals.” “If there are no consequences for actions taken under any guise, there will be no way to rebuild and reconcile. Peace cannot be built without justice.” “Those who have been displaced and whose communities or villages have been illegally occupied must be returned to their ancestral homes. Victims must also be compensated.” “If you look at the land-grabbing situation, land must be returned to its rightful owners. “ “This is the process of rebuilding. There must be compensation, the proper procedure must be followed, and any wrongdoing must result in a penalty. “The problems of justice administration in Nigeria require urgent attention in the form of reforms to address the majority of the issues impeding justice delivery.” “It is better for the country to recognise that we have a system that requires immediate intervention.” “For peace to reign, we must reorient our attitudes towards ourselves and others, particularly our brothers and sisters. I believe we should return to the basics, and this should be done intentionally.” He added, “Reconciliation must be deliberate and genuine. Regardless of what happened in Rwanda, they are back together because leaders and governments made a deliberate and intentional effort to bring people together. “I believe there is a need for deliberate and intentional reconciliation and peace-building, which can only be accomplished by government in collaboration with civil society organisations and religious leaders. “Many of these will be determined by our country’s elite.” In his welcome address, the Director-General of NIPSS, Prof. Ayo Omotayo, said, “Storytelling is a powerful instrument for peace-building and national reconciliation. “Societies are held together not only by laws and institutions but also by the stories citizens tell about themselves and one another.” “Stories shape our memories, influence how we understand our differences and imagine our common future.” “They can inspire solidarity, but when distorted or manipulated, they can deepen grievances and turn neighbours into enemies.” Also speaking, the former Chief Justice and Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Bage, said, “Conflict often begins long before violence erupts. item.title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
item.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends. But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare? What is El Niño? El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average. This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions. El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere. What does El Niño mean for Nigeria? NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy. For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall. These projections highlight the possibility of different weather outcomes across the country. 1. Higher temperatures and health risks One major concern is the possibility of increased heat. In October 2026, the Climate Impact Lab projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027, compared with an average year. The figure is a model-based estimate of potential excess deaths, not a confirmed death toll or a certainty that those deaths will occur. Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, particularly among children, older people and outdoor workers. Health authorities should strengthen public awareness campaigns, issue timely heat warnings and prepare health facilities for heat-related emergencies. item.title: 2027: Rise Networks, INEC, Meta, Google, Microsoft join forces to launch #AI4Elections Hackathon
item.description: Rise Networks, in collaboration with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Meta, Google, Microsoft and other partners, has launched the #AI4Elections Hackathon to develop artificial intelligence solutions aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. The national, multidisciplinary and nonpartisan initiative will bring together technology developers, researchers, university students, electoral experts, civil society organisations and innovators to develop practical AI-powered tools addressing challenges associated with elections. Other partners include the International Centre for Investigative Reporting (ICIR), NITHUB at the University of Lagos, the Centre for Information Technology and Development (CITAD), CLEEN Foundation, Tap Initiative for Citizens’ Development, International Press Centre, Legal Naija, Ahmadu Bello University and the Federal University of Technology, Akure. The programme is supported by the MacArthur Foundation and Luminate and builds on Rise Networks’ experience developing Run-Am, an AI-powered misinformation detection and fact-checking mobile application used during the 2023 Nigerian elections. Applications opened on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and will close on November 12 at 11:59 p.m. West African Time. The programme will run from October 2026 to February 2027, with a national grand finale and innovation showcase scheduled for December 16 in Lagos. Speaking at a press conference in Abuja, the founder of Rise Networks, Dr Toyosi Akerele-Ogunsiji, said the initiative was designed to promote responsible AI innovation that protects electoral integrity and citizens’ rights. “Our ambition is not to introduce technology for technology’s sake. We are committed to promoting responsible AI innovation that respects the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process, protects citizens’ rights, and prioritises transparency, privacy, and human oversight,” she said. “Innovation must strengthen our democracy, not create new vulnerabilities for it.” Akerele-Ogunsiji said Nigeria needed to harness emerging technologies to improve access to reliable information and strengthen public confidence in democratic institutions. “We must begin to harness the power of artificial intelligence to strengthen electoral integrity, expand access to information, and build greater public confidence in our democratic institutions,” she said. “The #AI4Elections Hackathon is an opportunity to bring our brightest minds together to develop solutions that respond to the realities of our electoral process.” The competition will focus on five principal areas: trustworthy electoral information; electoral data analysis, operational insights and decision support; inclusive and multilingual electoral and civic technology; electoral cybersecurity and resilience; and election observation and citizen accountability. item.title: 2027: ADC dismisses APC’s 2m votes target for Tinubu in Jigawa‎
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa ‎The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has expressed confidence that its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State in the 2027 general elections, dismissing the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s target of delivering two million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as unrealistic. ‎The ADC candidate for Ringim/Taura Federal Constituency in Jigawa State, Hon. Shehu Sule Udi, stated this while reacting to the Jigawa APC’s declaration that it would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. ‎Udi argued that the number of registered voters in Jigawa State made the APC’s target questionable, describing the declaration as political propaganda. ‎According to him, figures displayed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) showed that Jigawa had 2,807,811 registered voters. ‎“This clearly shows that the party is just making propaganda,” he said. ‎“Look at how our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and other candidates in ADC are gaining support across Jigawa State every day. For somebody to tell you that they will deliver two million votes to Tinubu is ridiculous,” Udi stated. ‎He claimed that residents of the state were dissatisfied with the current administration because of the economic hardship facing Nigerians. ‎“People of Jigawa State are tired of this administration. They have suffered enough, and no reasonable person will vote for the APC in the coming election. ‎“Our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State with massive votes and defeat President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. ‎Udi maintained that the ADC remained a credible alternative capable of addressing the economic challenges facing the country. ‎He expressed confidence that the growing support for the party across Jigawa State would translate into electoral victory in 2027. ‎The ADC candidate spoke while welcoming defectors from other political parties in Ringim and Taura Local Government Areas, describing their decision to join the party as a boost to its political strength ahead of the elections. item.title: Ebola patient arrives in Switzerland, as Nigeria sustains surveillance
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Swiss authorities confirmed on Monday that Nigeria’s imported Ebola case and her spouse have arrived in Switzerland, where she is receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals while he remains in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Mohammadu Ali Pate, disclosed the development in a statement on his X handle. His words: “The Swiss authorities have confirmed that the patient and her spouse arrived safely in Switzerland today. She is receiving care at Geneva University Hospitals, while her spouse is in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. “In our telephone conversation, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider conveyed Switzerland’s appreciation for the care provided by Nigerian health professionals and the close cooperation between our authorities and the World Health Organisation that made the evacuation possible. “I thank the clinical and public-health teams in Nigeria and Switzerland, the NCDC, @BAG_OFSP_UFSP , @EDI_DFI and @WHONigeria for their cooperation, and wish the patient continued recovery. “Here in Nigeria, contact monitoring, investigation of alerts and other containment measures continue, with support from @AfricaCDC and @WHOAFRO . We will provide regular updates through @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria,” he stated. The post Ebola patient arrives in Switzerland, as Nigeria sustains surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: INEC seeks inclusive polls, sensitises PWDs, Electoral Officers in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Benue State has held a sensitisation workshop for Persons With Disabilities (PWDs), Electoral Officers (EOs) and Disability Desk Officers, targeting improved accessibility, effective deployment of assistive devices and inclusive participation in the 2027 general elections. The workshop, organised by the commission ahead of the elections, was designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of disability inclusion, electoral rights and interventions aimed at ensuring that eligible voters with disabilities can participate fully in the electoral process. Speaking at the event, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC was committed to engaging stakeholders to ensure the conduct of free, fair and credible elections, stressing that inclusivity was equally essential to achieving that objective. The REC said, “it is not just to have free, fair and credible elections. It is to have inclusive elections. If you leave a chunk of your population out, you cannot be talking about free, fair and credible elections.” He added that INEC had a dedicated department responsible for inclusivity and addressing the concerns of disadvantaged groups to ensure everyone had the opportunity to participate in the electoral process. He explained that the commission identifies voters with disabilities during registration to enable it determine the needs of different polling units and deploy appropriate materials and assistance noting that “the objective is to ensure that eligible voters who have registered and obtained their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) did not encounter unnecessary difficulties while voting.” On the participation of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), the REC disclosed that INEC had conducted registration exercises at IDP locations in collaboration with non-governmental organisations interested in encouraging voter registration. He said “our officials visited the locations on two consecutive days to register eligible voters to ensure that they exercise their franchise during the election.” Addressing concerns over the collection of PVCs, Idris said “cards belonging to those who registered during the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise, conducted between August and December 2025, are available for collection at the local government level.” He added that cards for those who registered in 2026 would be ready subsequently before the elections. In his goodwill message, the Benue State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Comrade Mark Dewua, commended INEC for the initiative, saying “inclusive electoral participation is essential to strengthening democracy.” He urged for “accessible polling units, effective communication of electoral information, appropriate deployment of assistive devices and respectful treatment of voters with disabilities.” Dewua, who reaffirmed NOA’s commitment to collaborating with

item.title: 2027: INEC puts preliminary voters’ register online, publishes final document Dec. 15
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has made the Preliminary Register of Voters for the 2027 General Election available on its online platform, following concerns raised by some stakeholders and in preparation for the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on December 15. The register can now be accessed at https://display.inecnigeria.org. It is the same list that was earlier displayed at Registration Areas nationwide. National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said in a statement on Monday that the Commission “has taken note of the concerns expressed by Nigerians and other stakeholders regarding the desirability of making the Register accessible through its online platform in addition to the physical display already conducted.” “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform https://display.inecnigeria.org the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” he said. Haruna recalled that the physical display was held in accordance with Section 19 of the Electoral Act, 2026, from 9th to 15th October, 2026. According to him, the exercise provided “registered voters the opportunity to inspect their particulars and submit claims and objections as prescribed by law.” He said the online publication does not replace the exercise already carried out. “This additional measure complements the physical display already undertaken and is intended to facilitate wider public access to the Register,” he said. The Commission said it is still processing the claims and objections that arose from the display. “Meanwhile, the Commission continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026. “The Commission appreciates the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and stakeholders and reiterates its commitment to transparency, accountability and the faithful implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026 in delivering credible elections,” he said.
